absent: Send queue layout, its NAPI policy and its statistics structure are not shown in these fragments.
Virtqueue descriptor management, feature negotiation and control command wire formats are not shown.
XDP and AF_XDP pool setup, program attach lifecycle and redirect target handling are not shown.
RSS key and indirection programming sequences and offload negotiation are not shown.
Page pool initialization, DMA mapping lifecycle and socket-buffer allocator internals are not shown.
Configuration-space change handling, failover, ethtool programming and affinity hint handling are not shown.

findings.text: Receive queue state bundles a virtqueue reference with polling, filtering and accounting context: NAPI instance, RCU-guarded XDP program, receive stats, notification counter, dynamic moderation flag plus its mutex and moderator object, per-poll packet counter, coalescing settings, a singly linked spare page list, mergeable-buffer length estimator, page pool pointer with a flag for pool-owned DMA mapping, a scatter list sized for fragments plus linear and header entries, a minimum buffer length, a short textual name, XDP receive info plus AF_XDP pool, extra XSK receive info and XSK buffer table.

Device context keeps virtio device, control virtqueue, network device, transmit and receive queue arrays and status word, maximum and current queue-pair counts plus XDP pair count and enable flag, big-packet and mergeable-buffer modes with fragment count, RSS presence, hash reporting, key size, table size and supported versus saved hash types, control-queue presence with its mutex, header scatter capability and header length, transmit and receive tunnel flags including receive checksum, config-space and receive-mode work items with an enable flag, affinity-hint flag, two CPU hotplug list nodes, control buffer pointer, duplex and speed, receive moderation enable with transmit and receive coalescing settings, guest offload masks, failover pointer, device stats capability, RSS config header pointer and trailing hash key storage ending in a flexible array.
Control transaction buffer pairs a control header with an acknowledgement status field.

Transmit header helpers provide a hash header followed by alignment padding so the following data starts aligned, a common header union offering four views for plain, mergeable, hashed and tunnel variants, and a single static instance reserved for AF_XDP transmit.
Transmit buffer tag mask covers the lowest two address bits, supporting four completion kinds.
AF_XDP transmit length encoding shifts the tagged pointer right by two to recover byte length.
Mergeable receive context reserves the high bits for headroom by shifting that value left by twenty two, leaving the low twenty two bits for true size.
Transmit completions distinguish four buffer owners called socket buffer, orphaned socket buffer, XDP frame and AF_XDP, selected by the low tag bits carried in the completion token.

Queue numbering interleaves receive and transmit: even virtqueue indices map to receive queues and odd to transmit, with arithmetic converting in both directions; a classifier reports control type for the index equal to twice the maximum pair count, otherwise transmit for odd and receive for even.

RSS configuration sizes derive from live capability: header size spans the indirection table for the programmed table length or a single entry when RSS is absent, and trailer size spans the hash key for the programmed key length.
Receive-path moderation mutex serializes updates to the dynamic moderation enable flag and the associated coalescing parameters.
Control virtqueue mutex serializes control-queue commands.
Receive-mode work enable flag is mutated only while holding the RTNL mutex, with separate helpers to set and clear it.
Transmit and receive statistics updates are bracketed by sequence-counter begin and end markers around byte, packet, wake, stop and drop increments.

Spare receive pages form a singly linked stack through the page private field; retrieval pops the head and clears linkage while return splices a whole chain onto the head, falling back to fresh allocation when empty; buffer release returns to that stack when no page pool exists and otherwise returns the head page to the pool.

Scheduling checks readiness then suppresses callbacks before queuing NAPI; completion re-arms callbacks and, if NAPI finished, either reschedules on newly arrived work or reports done, otherwise keeps callbacks suppressed; AF_XDP completion notifies the pool then wakes NAPI unless already scheduled, disabling bottom halves around the schedule.

Transmit reclamation repeatedly polls completed tokens, decodes the owner tag and then consumes socket buffers with NAPI-aware release while counting bytes and packets separately for normal versus orphaned paths, returns XDP frames after measuring length, and accumulates AF_XDP byte length plus completion count before reporting completed bytes to the queue and signalling AF_XDP completions.
Transmit submission tags the completion token with the owner kind and enqueues the scatter list atomically; DMA scatter entries record address and length through accessor helpers.

Transmit queue flow control stops the queue when free descriptors fall below fragments plus two, counting stop events, and on the full path either re-arms delayed callbacks with NAPI rescheduling or, without NAPI, reclaims completions and restarts the queue with wake accounting when space recovered; a separate wake helper restarts a stopped queue while counting wake events.

Mergeable context packs headroom and true size into one opaque token with complementary decoders; validation derives required reservation from headroom plus shared-info allowance when headroom is present, aligned, and rejects frames whose length exceeds true size minus reservation while counting a receive length error.

Receive construction adjusts for header length and padding differences between mergeable and padded modes, then either builds a buffer in place for large aligned frames while recycling chained pages or copies small frames into a fresh allocation and attaches the remainder as fragments; mergeable mode adds at most one fragment or releases the page to the pool, while chained mode appends page fragments until exhausted and recycles leftovers, finally copying the device header into socket-buffer control storage.

AF_XDP receive sizing uses the pool frame size for the first buffer and adds header length for continuation buffers, rejecting oversize lengths with an error count and freeing the buffer; first buffers record length while later buffers initialize data pointers with headroom reduced by header length; socket-buffer construction from XDP copies metadata and payload into a fresh allocation, restores metadata offset when present and frees the source; small-packet path runs the XDP program under RCU and either passes to that construction, forwards transmit or redirect without a buffer, or drops with a counter.

Raw XDP queue test reports true only for the trailing slice of active pairs sized by the XDP pair count; polled receive retrieval asserts page-pool mode and returns buffer plus context; unmap-free routes AF_XDP buffers to XDP release and other buffers to the receive-queue free path selected by queue index.

XDP verdict handling counts every program result, passes through unchanged, converts transmit verdicts to frames and emits them while flagging transmit activity and mapping conversion or submission failures to drops with exception tracing, performs redirect while flagging redirect activity and mapping failure to drop, and treats abort, unknown actions and explicit drop as drops with warnings or tracing as appropriate.
Transmit interrupt entry suppresses further callbacks then either schedules transmit NAPI when polling is weighted or directly wakes the transmit queue.
Public helper re-enables delayed callbacks on a virtqueue, first short-circuiting broken devices to true and clearing a latched event flag before delegating to the transport-specific implementation.
If the virtqueue is marked broken, callback re-enable reports success without polling device state so callers leave reclamation cycles rather than looping without progress.

Oversize receive lengths are treated as length errors: the offending buffer is discarded or freed, a device-level length error counter is incremented, and processing returns failure or null rather than accepting truncated data.
